description: Green Loop used IESVE to assess a two-level laboratory complex in Colombia, including a basement. The case describes canopy shading and daylight studies, thermal-mass and ground-contact effects, and alternative HVAC configurations. Air drawn through a basement corridor was modelled as a supply plenum. The provider reports a 14% cooling-load reduction for that intake strategy compared with taking air directly from outside. The laboratory is unnamed. The listing location is Bogota, but the narrative specifies a hot, humid Colombian climate; an exact site location is not inferred. This public HTML case narrative is published by IES and can be read without payment. Its reuse licence is not stated. Access to the described software, input data and project models is not established by the public page. The source does not give a complete study period or all spatial and temporal model resolutions. Reported results are provider claims and have not been independently reproduced. The case supports the documented infrastructure simulation use and is linked to the named modelling resources. Only metadata and the case description were inspected; no data or model files were downloaded.
